publicationStmt.p: Amores Project working transcription, 9 September 2026. Independently source-reviewed by a second agent; not human-approved.

handDesc.handNote: Brown main writing and darker interventions are visible. Ink differences are recorded without assigning historical hands.

origin.p: The supplied library manifest dates the manuscript to the 10th/11th century; this does not date individual interventions.

surrogates.p: Library digital facsimile, PPN1844735508. The supplied manifest identifies the images as Public Domain Mark 1.0. Every verse in folios 66v, 67r was inspected for this first pass.

projectDesc.p: Source-grounded transcription of all 52 manuscript verses, independently checked against the images. No other witness or normalized edition was used as transcription input. Existing annotation coordinates provide navigation, not text. There are 104 annotation rows for 52 distinct source verses. Each duplicate pair has identical page and bounds. The last existing row per verse was selected and every resulting rectangle was inspected. All original bounds remain unchanged; some regions include neighbouring text or exclude additions. sourceWitness=LL and panelId are provenance only, not transcription input.

correction.p: Uncertain letters are marked unclear and unreadable text gap. Darker ink is hi, not proof of erasure or a distinct hand. Actual additions use add; deletion or substitution is asserted only with visible evidence and qualified where needed. No unattested earlier reading is supplied.

normalization.p: Single source-oriented display. Ordinary allographs and long s are represented with standard Latin characters. Source spelling is preserved; word spacing and couplet layout are editorial. Explicit abbreviation expansions remain in TEI choices. Punctuation and unusual signs are schematic typographic equivalents, not exact pen-shape replicas.

punctuation.p: Visible significant punctuation and separation or insertion marks are retained. No modern sentence punctuation is supplied.

segmentation.p: Each l is one verse and one physical source line. Full-page inspection of folios66v and67r shows alternate physical lines inset, recorded on even verses; the larger O at verse35 is retained as an initial, within the continuous source sequence. The lg groups are editorial elegiac couplets. Each verse has a stable ID and an existing facsimile rectangle. The rectangles may include neighbouring text and need not enclose marginal inscriptions.

interpretation.p: Every note has received an independent second source reading. The companion ledger distinguishes supported observations from documented source uncertainty; none is assigned to human review.

revisionDesc.change: Independently read all 52 source verses and every first-pass note, checked full-page insets and selected duplicated rectangle provenance. Added supported points and previously unencoded source marks, preserving textual readings and local uncertainty.
First source pass covering all 52 verses and visible interventions in folios 66v, 67r; awaiting a different agent's independent reading.

div.head: Independently reviewed source notes
div.note: Independent enlarged-source reading confirms the following evidence: An ornamental M opens the poem. The t of patientia is darker; no former letter is supplied.
Independent enlarged-source reading confirms the following evidence: A short dark horizontal stroke crosses the pecto/re interval. Its function is unspecified; the readable word is retained.
Independent enlarged-source reading confirms the following evidence: The et ligature closes Scilicet. Source adserui is retained.
Independent enlarged-source reading confirms the following evidence: The source writes que with e rather than an expanded ae spelling. The final et of pudet is a ligature.
Independent enlarged-source reading confirms the following evidence: The source verb is calcimus. No u or other correction is supplied.
Independent enlarged-source reading confirms the following evidence: An i is added above between p and t in capti, with a small caret beneath. The physical addition is retained separately.

Independent enlarged-source reading confirms the following evidence: The t at the end of et and d of proderit are darker. A vertical mark crosses the Perfer/et boundary; its function is unspecified. Word separation is editorial.
Independent enlarged-source reading confirms the following evidence: A vertical stroke crosses the tam/saepe boundary. It is retained without asserting cancellation of either word.
Independent enlarged-source reading confirms the following evidence: A question-like sign closes the line.
Independent enlarged-source reading confirms the following evidence: The visible sequence is nescio cui quem tu complexa tenebas; the word separation is editorial.

Independent enlarged-source reading confirms the following evidence: The source reads seruus followed by an et ligature. Ut is written above the ligature and again in the right margin. All three written components are preserved without asserting cancellation of the ligature.

The darker final i of Vidi and first l of lassus are supported. A slender oblique stroke lies to the right between the ends of 13 and 14; it is now represented as a marginal mark attached to 13 for navigation, without asserting punctuation or cancellation.
Independent enlarged-source reading confirms the following evidence: The source reads adesi. The t of patienter is dark; a question-like sign closes the line.
Independent enlarged-source reading confirms the following evidence: The baseline tuis has a dot below i and u above it. This expunction/substitution is retained. Points divide the three clauses.
Independent enlarged-source reading confirms the following evidence: Et ligatures close Scilicet and supply the following conjunction.
Independent enlarged-source reading confirms the following evidence: The o-region of amori is dark. The visible ending is retained without adding a final s.
Independent enlarged-source reading confirms the following evidence: A tall dark stroke crosses the mendacia/linguae boundary. It is an unspecified mark, not an asserted cancellation.
Independent enlarged-source reading confirms the following evidence: A short horizontal stroke appears below the r-region of periuratos. It is recorded schematically; dampna is preserved as written.
Independent enlarged-source reading confirms the following evidence: Dis simulata has editorial word separation; the visible letters and terminal question-like sign are retained.
Independent enlarged-source reading confirms the following evidence: Egr in egra is dark. The source has egra here and aegra in the following verse; the differing spelling is retained.

Independent enlarged-source reading confirms the following evidence: The visible sequence is Venet ri uali, with an et ligature and a vertical stroke at that boundary. It is retained without normalizing it to a familiar reading. The a of erat is dark.
The source has separate dark letters et, que and duraui. Two terminal dark points are now represented schematically by a colon-like sign; their pen positions are not reproduced typographically.

The source has qui ista pati with a dark point/oblique stroke above the i-region and a caret beneath that boundary. Velit is above the line to the right, with another small caret below its opening. Both carets and the previously unencoded dark mark are now represented. The internal mark does not establish cancelled baseline letters.
Independent enlarged-source reading confirms the following evidence: The i of redimita is dark. Its preceding d is retained as visible, without inferring an erased earlier word.
Independent enlarged-source reading confirms the following evidence: The e of tumescentis is dark. No erased state is reconstructed.
Independent enlarged-source reading confirms the following evidence: Source condam is retained, and the et conjunction is a ligature.

Independent enlarged-source reading confirms the following evidence: A vertical stroke follows Perdere. Ut on the baseline is dark and another ut appears in the right margin; both are preserved without asserting a link to another verse.

A larger O and faint looped/oblique left-margin strokes are visible beside this couplet. The margin mark, formerly only described in a note, is now encoded schematically with an illegible-sign description. Its function is uncertain; no additional modern poem division or hand is imposed.
Independent enlarged-source reading confirms the following evidence: The source has hodit with initial h. The final et of habet is a ligature.

Independent enlarged-source reading confirms the following evidence: The ending io of fugio is dark. Reducet ends with an et ligature, and it is added above that ending. The source layers are retained without declaring the ligature cancelled.
Direct source inspection shows vertical strokes at both sine/te and nec/tecum. The second previously omitted boundary stroke is now encoded. Neither securely establishes cancellation.

The s-region of formosa has horizontal and dotted dark strokes. The qualified current s is retained and the visible marks are now encoded explicitly with unspecified function. Their earlier letter content or definite cancellation remains uncertain; initial m of the first minus is dark.

Independent enlarged-source reading confirms the following evidence: The visible verb is fact, without a separate i. Final s of mores and initial t of tam are dark. No silent correction to expected grammar is supplied.
Independent enlarged-source reading confirms the following evidence: Precor is contracted as barred p plus cor, with darker cor; the expansion is explicit. Socialia is dark and remains readable.
Independent enlarged-source reading confirms the following evidence: A slender stroke follows instar. It is retained as an unspecified metamark.

Independent enlarged-source reading confirms the following evidence: The first Quid has a dot below d and c above, encoded as a substitution. Ui is dark with s raised above its end; initial e and g of elige are dark. All visible components are retained without assigning hands.
Independent enlarged-source reading confirms the following evidence: Initial u of uelle and a of amem are darker. No earlier state is supplied.

Independent enlarged-source reading confirms the following evidence: A compact barred group above Ut qui appears q with a bar followed by qudm. It remains an unclear unexpanded abbreviation. The baseline Ut qui si nolim is retained. Tamen is dark; a terminal colon-like mark and stroke precede the ornamental Q opening3.12.

back.note: A terminal point after latus is visible in the fresh enlargement and is now retained; the reading Inualidum referens emeritumque latus is unchanged.
A terminal point follows illo in the full source and fresh enlargement. It is now encoded; the source wording remains unchanged.
